name: MonarchAiSlashCommands
title: AiSlashCommands
wrapsNative: MonarchSlashMenu (a VStack of Button rows in the bottom safeAreaInset above the prompt) driven by MonarchSlashMenuQuery.find(in:trigger:position: .wordStart) on the prompt's text binding
summary: The / command menu of an assistant prompt: typing a slash shows commands such as /summarize above the prompt, filtered as you type, and choosing one rewrites the typed command.
whenToUse: Above an assistant prompt or composer that offers commands such as /summarize, /translate or /search.
whenNotToUse: For inserting blocks in a document editor use MonarchSlashMenu. For @ mentions use the mentions of MonarchMessageComposer (MonarchMentionPicker). For starting suggestions in an empty conversation use MonarchAiStarterPrompts.
api: init(text: Binding<String>, commands: [MonarchSlashMenuItem], trigger: Character = "/", groupOrder: [String] = [], labels: MonarchSlashMenuLabels = MonarchSlashMenuLabels(), onSelect: @escaping @MainActor (MonarchSlashMenuItem) -> String?)

options.name: text
options.description: The prompt's text. The menu reads the command being typed (a slash at the start of a word) and writes the result back.

options.name: commands
options.description: Every command. label is the name typed after the slash, with or without the slash; description, systemImage, group, keywords and isDisabled are used as in MonarchSlashMenu.

options.name: trigger
options.description: The character that opens the menu.

options.name: groupOrder
options.description: Group headings in display order, for commands with a group.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the list name ("Commands"), the empty text ("No commands match “/x”") and the count ("3 commands").

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Receives the chosen command (as passed in commands) and returns the text that replaces the typed /query, or nil to remove it and run the command at once.

states.name: closed
states.description: No command is being typed: nothing is drawn.

states.name: open
states.description: A slash at the start of a word: every command, with its icon, /name and description.

states.name: filtered
states.description: Names that start with the query first, then names that contain it, then matches in descriptions and keywords.

states.name: disabled command
states.description: Shown in the disabled colours and cannot be chosen.

appearance: A full-width strip on the surface background with a subtle top border; names in strong body text, descriptions muted, icons in the muted icon colour; disabled rows use the disabled text role. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web hook wires a listbox beside the caret of AiPromptInput, with focus kept in the textarea and Arrow keys, Enter and Tab to choose; iOS gives no caret position, so the menu is the MonarchSlashMenu strip above the prompt and each command is a button. The web takes a separate AiSlashCommand type; iOS reuses MonarchSlashMenuItem, with label as the command name. The web's combineAiPromptMenus is not needed: put this strip and the composer's mention picker in the same inset. Escape to dismiss has no touch equivalent: typing a space or deleting the slash closes the menu. Android uses the same name and options.
accessibility: The list is a container named "Commands" (labels.label).
Each command is a button read as its /name and its description; disabled commands are not activatable.
The number of commands, or the empty text, is announced as it changes, so focus can stay in the prompt.
Rows are at least 44 points high and grow with Dynamic Type; icons are decorative.
edgeCases: A slash inside a word (and/or) does not open the menu; a space after the command closes it.
Queries longer than 24 characters close the menu (MonarchSlashMenuQuery's maxLength).
Return text ending in a space, such as "/summarize ", so the menu closes after the choice.
Command ids must be unique: the chosen row is matched back to the command by id.

examples.title: Insert the command
examples.setup:
@State private var prompt = "/"

private let commands = [
    MonarchSlashMenuItem(id: "summarize", label: "summarize", description: "Summarize the open document", systemImage: "list.bullet", keywords: ["shorten", "recap"]),
    MonarchSlashMenuItem(id: "rewrite", label: "rewrite", description: "Rewrite the selection in a different tone", systemImage: "pencil"),
    MonarchSlashMenuItem(id: "search", label: "search", description: "Search connected documents", systemImage: "magnifyingglass"),
    MonarchSlashMenuItem(id: "schedule", label: "schedule", description: "Needs a calendar connection", systemImage: "calendar", isDisabled: true),
]
